prompt_en: A complex performance photograph of a fictional adult performer in a dry, glass-enclosed recital hall below the sea. She prepares to sing, lips parted on a quiet intake of breath, with one hand steadying an open score before its first note. Use the supplied portrait as a visible facial-appearance reference: large brown eyes, fine gently curved eyebrows, a small rounded nose, softly curved lips and a rounded jawline. Her presentation conveys a warm, composed presence; the face retains subtle skin texture. Two thick black corkscrew ponytails are rooted separately at the two sides of her head and fall beside her shoulders as tapered helixes with several open turns. A separate narrow silver satin ribbon winds around the outside of each black hair spiral on successive turns; little tied ribbon ends remain visible at the top. She wears a dark navy fitted stage dress with a knee-length flared skirt. Its detached navy sleeves begin below the upper arms and flare to the wrists, with an exposed band of skin separating each sleeve from the bodice. Thin raised coral piping traces the neckline, bodice panel seams and sleeve cuffs, visibly contrasting with the navy cloth. Her right forearm extends towards a waist-high music stand on her right; right fingertips rest on the lower edge of the score page. Her left arm hangs a little clear of her torso. Both feet in low ankle boots rest on the timber stage, set apart for a balanced upright stance. Curved window mullions enclose blue seawater, drifting kelp and a school of small fish outside. Concentric brass resonator rings hang behind the stage. An audience-level vertical full-length view shows the front of the bodice and both sleeve gaps, with room around both hair coils. Warm stage light gives the face a quiet glow against late-afternoon blue water, while broken water-light patterns touch the floor. Natural perspective and tangible satin, hair and glass textures hold the image as a believable directed editorial photograph.
